thesis: The Garden City Company is a closely held farmland and royalty company headquartered in Garden City, Kansas, with a secondary office in Colorado Springs. **[Fact]** The company owns farmland in southwest Kansas that it leases to tenant farmers on an annual **crop-share** basis: revenue is recognized when crops are harvested and inventoried, and grain inventory on the balance sheet represents the company's share of unsold crops. **[Fact]** It also collects **oil and gas royalties** from wells operated by third parties on its land. **[Fact]** As of December 31, 2024, **34,865** shares were outstanding; stockholders' equity was **$14.2 million** (**~$407** per share). **[Fact]** The company carries **no bank debt**, invests surplus cash in U.S. Treasury and equity securities (**$8.1 million** fair value at year-end 2024), and pays a large annual cash dividend (**$40** per share in 2024, **$45** in 2023). **[Fact]** Leadership includes President and CEO R. Thayer Tutt, Jr. and a board chaired by William J. Hybl; the stock trades OTC Pink (GCCO) with audited GAAP financials posted via OTC Markets.
why_market_wrong: The market may treat GCCO as an illiquid family dividend stub, either ignoring the **embedded liquid-asset and farmland bundle** or overpaying after a multi-year move above book value. **[Fact]** At an indicative **~$1,284** per share (December 2024 stock option exercise price), the stock trades roughly **3.2 times** December 2024 GAAP book (**~$407** per share) and about **4 times** mark-to-market liquid assets (cash, securities, and grain inventory, **~$317** per share combined). **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **family-controlled farmland OTC** plus **market structure discount** (no exchange listing, thin volume, dividend screens only). **[Inference]** Land and water rights are carried at **historical cost** (**$2.93 million** on the balance sheet); supplemental acreage schedules in older PDFs were not text-extracted in this workspace, so economic farmland value may exceed GAAP but is **[Assumption]** until verified. **[Inference]** FY2024 farm rental and oil/gas revenues fell versus 2023 on crop and commodity prices, so trailing earnings understate mid-cycle cash generation but also show cyclical risk.
